note: BUMPED to 1.0.10 from 1.0.9. THE TRANSCRIPTION, THE SECTION MODEL AND THE ANCHORS ARE UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.9’s (sha256 748e58cef10981193585a101fcf67951cc3a37577eaf756f08399e343e1dd8bf), and divisions.json and base.json are carried unchanged. THREE THINGS MOVE, and none of them is the text of the print. (1) TWO READINGS ARE CORRECTED: r8653 served "that which is delicious food," where the print sets a Greek word and the bracketed gloss [delicious food] — the rule deleted the print’s Greek word and invented English filler — and r11652 served a dangling apostrophe where the print sets "not only" and a superscript footnote marker. Both are withdrawn and their corrected readings appended as r11900 and r11901. (2) 83 REVIEW FLAGS ARE CLEARED: at each, an independent witness carries the rule’s WHOLE `after` reading at the point — for 73 of them the two other scans of the same 1816 print the library already ingested, whose own _djvu.xml keeps PUNCTUATION AND CASE (the instrument the re-flowed Gutenberg witness does not have, and the reason the marks-and-case class could not be decided before), for 10 of them a scan together with the human-proofread transcription. (3) 9 rules carry the two copies’ own reading in their `witness` with the flag KEPT: at those points the print carries the very form the rule changes, so the rule is an emendation of the print’s own form and not a repair of a scan error. MEASURED over all 809 OCR-typed review-flagged rules: 470 stand in vol. I, the only volume the two other scans carry; of those, 73 are confirmed by both scans on the whole reading (with our own context on both sides, case and marks included), 142 by one scan, 10 are contradicted by both, 28 by one, 32 the two scans disagree on and 185 neither could decide. Nothing else in the record is touched.
citation: Proclus, On the Theology of Plato, trans. Thomas Taylor (London, 1816). The Neoplatonic Library, version 1.0.10. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23242773. https://neoplatonic-library.org/texts/proclus-theology-of-plato-taylor-1816/
